save_and_failure_flow_review.conflict: Read actual bytes in unique parse path, compare both stored model and committed bytes; check unchanged bytes before and immediately before QSaveFile commit under shared cooperative lock.
save_and_failure_flow_review.atomic_commit: No direct-write fallback; encoded size/read errors, open/write/commit errors return false; only successful write updates committed bytes/model.
save_and_failure_flow_review.gui: Busy disables controls, error clears busy while preserving draft, saved signal renders committed snapshot then emits GUI-side completion; toggling only changes visibility and preserves both draft pairs; requestLeave covers busy and continue/discard.
save_and_failure_flow_review.limitations: Cooperation requires same lock path among writers. Noncooperating external writers can still race after final compare; no stronger atomic compare-and-swap claim is made.

qt5_lock_followup.verified_semantics: Destructor invokes unlock. Unix unlock closes fd first and clears ownership/error state even when unlink fails. Retrying unlock on that object cannot retry deletion. Default30s mtime staleness also applies while PID remains alive; Qt stale removal uses an auxiliary rmlock and native lock protection.
qt5_lock_followup.safe_choice: Dedicated precreated lock subdirectory shared by all callers avoids this observed parent0500 write-bit-loss case without ad-hoc deletion. Retaining an object after failed unlock is ineffective; retaining it without ever unlocking would need a new long-lived lock/exit protocol.
qt5_lock_followup.not_recommended: No QFile::remove, PID-only deletion, forced removeStaleLockFile or shortened staleness used as normal retry shortcut.
qt5_lock_followup.remaining_limit: Revoking write access on the lock directory itself, or traversal rights on its ancestors, can still prevent cleanup and require Qt's normal stale recovery. Do not claim universal immediate recovery after arbitrary permission changes.
